text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer. When identifying bugs, the first step is to understand exactly what the program is doing wrong. Are there error messages? Does it crash, or does it simply give the wrong result? Once you know the problem, you can use debugging tools such as breakpoints and step-by-step execution to find where things go wrong. A systematic approach is important: change one thing at a time and test again, so you always know what caused the difference. Logging is also very useful, because it records what the program was doing before the error happened. With patience and good habits, most bugs can be found and fixed.
